principle: Long-form narrative interpretation and memory consolidation are model-owned semantic work. Derived observations remain source-bound, invalidatable and non-authoritative.

narrative.world.purpose: Interpret source-bound long-horizon narrative state without treating derived memory as authority.
rubric: Use only source-bound records visible at the supplied narrative cutoff.
Keep event occurrence time distinct from narration/reveal time.
Track who knows what and when, setup/payoff state, relationship evolution, obligations and causal links when supported by evidence.
Never use future active-plan/review/proposal information as current Canon unless the caller explicitly requests planning context.
Return typed derived observations with source refs; derived observations are not Canon.

Propose only facts actually supported by exact quotes from the final candidate_text. Drafting plans and pre-draft character proposals cannot establish final story facts. An empty changes array is valid.

For existing entities copy the exact supplied entity_ref. For a new entity use a unique local:<label> reference, including local references in relationship participants and character knowledge. Core assigns durable ids and before-state hashes.

Choose the output_contract oneOf branch matching entity_type. Its fields schema is the complete and exclusive writable field contract; every required field must be present and no extra field is allowed. Timeline and knowledge orders cannot exceed current_story_order.

Return complete replacement fields for any updated entity, preserving its supplied writable fields unless the final candidate supports a change. The entity_ref, source_fingerprint and source_metadata are read-only identity/provenance, not replacement fields; do not copy them into fields or invent new provenance. Never delete entities, infer hidden character thoughts as established facts, or write Canon yourself.

reader.expectations.purpose: Interpret which reader-facing questions, promises, setups, relationship expectations, goals or mysteries are currently live and how much pressure they carry.
rubric: Derive expectations only from supplied reader-facing evidence and accepted/locked story history unless planning context is explicitly requested.
Separate an expectation existing in the reader experience from a future planned payoff.
Identify meaningful reinforcement, partial reward, payoff, abandonment or dormancy; do not demand mechanical cliffhangers.
Prefer reader-experience language over author-process language.
Return proposals for ledger updates; the model judgment itself does not mutate Canon.
Each update must quote exact text from candidate_text and cite candidate:<candidate_fingerprint>. A plan is not evidence of a payoff. Empty expectation_updates is valid when no change is supported.

Use expected_version 0 for a new expectation; its local expectation_id will be replaced by a Core identity. For an existing expectation, copy its exact id and version. Do not invent an existing expectation.
Return at most one update for each existing expectation_id in this observation. Combine the interpretation into one supported operation rather than repeating an id for touch, partial or paid changes.
For an open operation, omit due_by_order when no deadline is supported; if supplied, due_by_order must be at least current_reading_order, never earlier than the chapter that opens it.
These are model proxy observations, never measured reader retention or real reader feedback.

reader.pressure.purpose: Prepare source-bound predictions of reader questions, possible rewards and delay costs from the chapter brief, prior live expectations, explicit reading position and resolved writer-safe causal trace; this proposal cannot prove effects in prose that has not yet been read.
rubric: Identify what a reader has reason to care about, what concrete reward this chapter can provide, and the cost of delaying it. Ground each pressure point in supplied source_ref identities.

Use the explicitly supplied genre_profile, platform_profile, chapter_position and reader_grip to weigh the proposal. Missing positioning is a limit, not permission to invent a platform formula or to treat a private author preference as reader-observed evidence.

Distinguish intended reader effects from effects supported by accepted prior prose. Plans remain plans; reader expectation observations remain model proxies. status=pass means only a usable pre-draft proposal, not a passed Reader audit, realized reward, demonstrated reading value or production release.

Source binding verifies where a prediction came from, not whether a reader felt it. Only a later reading of the actual candidate can judge realization; do not present expected rewards, proposed_net_change or next_chapter_pull as effects already delivered by unwritten prose.

Preserve supported character choices, observable responses, consequences and uncertainty from the causal trace. Anticipate why they may matter without turning the trace into an equal-weight step report or a paragraph template. Do not invent a cost that changes no option or consequence; if no material delay cost is supported, say so.

A quiet chapter, specialized procedure or restrained scene can provide relationship, emotional, informational, competence, contemplative or atmospheric value. Do not force conflict, cliffhangers, quotas of events or emotion, fixed reward frequency or a universal beat template; an empty pressure_points array is valid when the evidence supports no discrete pressure point.
Do not invent measurable retention rates, real reader reactions or unsupported attraction scores.
Keep the output compact and usable by the Writer. Do not copy private character state, author explanations or final manuscript prose.

memory.consolidate.purpose: Propose compact derived memory from bounded accepted/project-provided evidence without replacing source authority.
rubric: Summarize only supplied evidence; preserve uncertainty and source references.
Prefer details likely to matter to current/future story reasoning rather than exhaustive recap.
Do not convert plans, proposals, reviews, research truth or model inference into accepted Canon.
Every derived item must remain invalidatable/rebuildable and cite its sources.
Return proposed derived-memory items only.
